title: Littlestone-dimension regret bounds for unrestricted classes
formal: Do universal real constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) exist such that, for every nonempty set \(\mathcal X\), every nonempty Boolean concept class \(\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\) of finite Littlestone dimension \(d\ge1\), and every integer horizon \(T\ge d\), the optimal adversarial online regret satisfies \[c\sqrt{dT}\le R_T(\mathcal H)\le C\sqrt{dT}?\] Here \[R_T(\mathcal H)=\inf_A\ \sup_{(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_T,y_T)\in\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell(p_t,y_t)-\min_{h\in\mathcal H}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbf1\{h(x_t)\ne y_t\}\right\},\] where \(p_t=A_t((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_{t-1},y_{t-1}),x_t)\in[0,1]\), \(\ell(p,0)=p\), and \(\ell(p,1)=1-p\). The infimum ranges over all such causal prediction rules. No restriction of countability, topology, compactness, or measurability is imposed on \(\mathcal X\) or \(\mathcal H\). The unresolved issue in the source is whether the upper bound holds with this full generality; the matching lower scale is already known.

source_formulation.text: Is \(\Theta(\sqrt{\operatorname{LD}(\mathcal H)T})\) the optimal adversarial binary online regret for arbitrary concept classes, without the extra minimax regularity condition?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase

why: Littlestone dimension already characterizes whether adversarial online classification is learnable. This question asks whether that single combinatorial number also controls the sharp regret for every class. Removing the remaining regularity assumption would complete that quantitative characterization; a counterexample would exhibit a genuine limitation of a purely dimension-based prediction theorem.
status_note: The 2024 source and Raman’s 2025 dissertation explicitly retain this unrestricted-class question. The checked 2021 sharp theorem relies on a minimax step later sources qualify; the May 2026 resource improvement retains logarithmic factors. No matching unrestricted resolution was found in the bounded search through 16 September 2026. This records the available source evidence, not a proof of present openness.

category_assignment.reason: The actual extracted question is a dimension-based optimal regret characterization for unrestricted concept classes in online classification.

importance.reason: A foundational quantitative characterization of adversarial binary learning, with universal scope over concept classes. The outstanding gap concerns the validity of the sharp dimension-only bound without a technical minimax assumption, rather than practical computational efficiency.

sentences: A learner predicts binary labels while an adversary supplies instances and then labels.
Its regret is the expected number of errors beyond those of the best fixed concept on the same sequence.
The question asks whether every class of finite Littlestone dimension has regret of square-root order in dimension times horizon, with universal constants.
The sharp known theorem uses a minimax regularity assumption, and later primary sources explicitly leave removal of that assumption open.
A complete Lean answer must establish the universal two-sided bound for arbitrary classes or refute it under the same prediction model.

definitions: A concept \(h\) assigns one binary label to every instance. A complete binary tree of depth \(r\) has one instance from \(\mathcal X\) at each internal node and its outgoing edges labeled 0 and 1. The tree is shattered by \(\mathcal H\) if every root-to-leaf path has a concept whose labels on that path's nodes equal its edge labels. The Littlestone dimension \(d\) is the largest shattered depth. Each horizon-specific rule \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_T)\) is an arbitrary family of set functions from labeled histories and the current instance to \([0,1]\); it may depend on the whole class and on \(T\). The number \(p_t\) is a probability of predicting label 1, so \(\ell(p_t,y_t)\) is the expected zero-one mistake loss. No probability distribution on the arbitrary instance space is required: regret is defined directly by the displayed supremum of finite sums. Equivalently, the adversary presents \(x_t\), the learner chooses \(p_t\), and the adversary then supplies \(y_t\); the charged loss is \(\ell(p_t,y_t)\), not an adversary's reaction to a sampled binary prediction. The learner sees the label before the next round. Future instances and labels are unavailable. The sequence need not be realizable by any concept; comparison is to the best single concept in hindsight. The minimum comparator loss exists because the class is nonempty and losses are integers in \(\{0,\ldots,T\}\). The infimum over rules and supremum over sequences need not be attained. Running time, memory, computability, and finite descriptions of the class or rules are unrestricted; the predictor need not choose a concept from the class. The constants must be independent of the domain, class, dimension, and horizon, and logarithmic factors may not be hidden. The restriction \(T\ge d\) is essential to this square-root formulation because regret is at most \(T\); the omitted dimension-zero case has a single distinct concept and zero regret.
answer_criterion: Prove the universal two-sided statement, or its logical negation, in Lean under the stated arbitrary-set prediction model. For a positive answer, supply universal constants and prove both bounds, using any previously formalized lower-bound result with matching hypotheses. If an optimal rule does not attain the infimum, rules approaching the upper bound arbitrarily closely suffice. A negative answer must refute the existence of universal constants: for every proposed pair \(0<c\le C<\infty\), some class and allowed horizon violate a bound. In view of the known universal lower bound, the outstanding mathematical task is the upper bound or classes with unbounded ratio \(R_T(\mathcal H)/\sqrt{dT}\). A result with a class-dependent constant, an extra logarithmic factor, or an added regularity hypothesis does not settle the question. This is an exact constant-factor asymptotic claim, not an additive numerical approximation.

context_blocks.text: In agnostic online classification, labels can contradict every member of the reference class. Regret therefore subtracts the errors of the best fixed concept instead of requiring the learner to make few errors outright. Randomized predictions are represented by their probabilities, which gives the stated finite-sum game even when the instance set has no measurable structure.

Littlestone dimension measures how long a class can sustain every binary answer pattern along an adaptively chosen tree of instances. Finite dimension characterizes online learnability. Here the question is quantitative: can the optimal cumulative excess error always be bounded by a universal constant times the square root of dimension times horizon?

The standard unrestricted binary bounds have lower scale \(\Omega(\sqrt{dT})\) and an upper bound with an additional logarithmic factor. Alon and coauthors obtain the sharp square-root rate through a connection with sequential Rademacher complexity. The later sources explicitly point out that the minimax step supporting this connection assumes an additional regularity condition on the class.

The source paper studies self-directed learning, where the learner chooses the order of available instances. Its footnote asks a separate question about the ordinary adversarial game. This card preserves that footnote’s question: the adversary supplies each next instance, and the dimension is Littlestone dimension rather than the paper’s self-directed dimension.

The 2023 multiclass paper explicitly records the unresolved unrestricted binary question and carries the same regularity condition into its sharp finite-label bounds. Raman’s 2025 dissertation repeats that qualification. It would therefore be incorrect to treat the unrestricted-looking headline of the 2021 theorem as a checked unconditional resolution.

The theorem on randomized Littlestone dimension and nearly realizable sequences cites the same 2021 upper bound inside its proof. It supplies no independent justification for removing the regularity condition. Its different mistake-budget formulation is not silently substituted for the present arbitrary-sequence regret target.

The checked May 2026 work improves weak-consistency-oracle complexity and memory in agnostic online learning. Its dimension-dependent regret guarantee still hides logarithmic factors. Those resource improvements do not supply the universal constant-factor upper bound requested here.
